To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the liver of grazing beef cows on low herbage allowances during winter gestation is a highly active organ that responds to the metabolic stress of energy deficit by increasing gluconeogenesis and fatty acids oxidation and by decreasing cell growth, DNA, and RNA replication, and transcription.
beef cows on grazing high HA of native pastures had better metabolic status during winter gestation and early spring lactation than cows on low HA.

the liver transcriptome of grazing beef cows on native grasslands is affected by days, HA and HA × genotype interactions, and the changes are consistent with a complex and previously unknown hepatic adaptive program.

understanding liver gene expression in beef cows on native grasslands, and the potential for improving the efficiency of beef cow-calf production systems.

beef cows on grazing high HA have a better hepatic adaptation to negative energy balance during winter gestation and early postpartum than cows grazing on lower HA.
the liver is an organ of great importance in the regulation of metabolic processes in beef cows, and that it is a key player in their adaptation to different nutritional environments.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the liver transcriptome of grazing beef cows is affected by HA, cow genotype, and their interaction, with the most important changes occurring during the winter gestation period.
the liver transcriptome of beef cows is highly responsive to nutritional changes during gestation and to the nutritional environment during lactation.
the liver transcriptome in beef cows grazing high HA is more similar to the transcriptome of beef cows in early lactation than to the transcriptome observed in beef cows in winter gestation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
beef cows on grazing high HA have a better metabolic status and liver transcriptome than cows grazing low HA.
the liver of beef cows on grazing is highly plastic and adapts to the environment in a complex manner, which is likely to have implications for animal performance.
beef cows are able to maintain a relatively stable liver transcriptome throughout pregnancy and early lactation, despite the negative energy balance experienced during winter and early lactation.
